scope: Bounded read-only CPU audit of a copied full Chicago source/resource snapshot, plus static renderer/traffic code review and read-only Metal adapter properties. No GPU command queue or dispatch was created by this audit.
findings: No capacity or indexing blocker in the audited snapshot. Night, always-on day and all five sampled dynamic light grids remain enabled; no fallback to a full linear light scan occurs.

Night grid uses 69.49% of the fixed cell budget and less than 1% of its index budget. Its maximum local list is164 lights; traffic adds at most9 in the sampled positions. Larger future geographic expansion should re-run this capacity check.

Combined vertex/material indexing remains safely below UInt32 limits. The largest scene buffer is3.865GB versus the actual M3 Ultra maxBufferLength373.662GB. Adapter properties are read-only capability evidence, not a GPU memory/performance benchmark.

MetalRenderer constructs the static city BLAS once. TrafficMetal writes only the15.53MB vehicle tail, refits/rebuilds only its161,812-triangle dynamic BLAS, and refits a two-instance TLAS. Periodic or large-scrub rebuilds never rebuild the40.10-million-triangle static city.

encodeUpdate returns without work when the absolute scene time is unchanged; several samples at one movie time share the same traffic update. The six lanes cap at28 vehicles each, giving168 vehicles and504 dynamic lights.

Static world bounds include the existing horizon planes at±50km. Maximum Float ULP there is3.906mm; Wrigley coordinates near8km retain submillimetre coordinate precision. The broad planes do not define the light grid, which is bounded by finite light ranges.
limitations: The root still owns actual GPU timing, Metal AS allocation/traversal performance, visual quality and final source/package equivalence. Existing first-package self-test succeeded on the M3 Ultra, but this CPU audit does not claim that its newer snapshot was dispatched on the GPU.

Five traffic clocks (0,60,240,-120,3600 seconds) sample dynamic grids; this is not an exhaustive proof over every possible clock. Seven conservative finite-support probes per light complement the existing dedicated LightGrid regression suite.
Reported per-grid CPU durations include construction, ordering/bounds checks and support-probe validation; they must not be treated as production per-frame CPU timing.
Concurrent authorized edits occurred after the copied snapshot. Changed files are listed below; this report remains tied to its sourceInputSHA256 and does not silently claim the final package.
